free_tier.stated: Free with no sign-up: a stable https://user-<n>.nport.link URL over HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket, served from Cloudflare's edge. The harness measured a 4-hour session cap and confirmed the CLI spawns a bundled cloudflared.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel; the harness measured a 4-hour session cap

egress.terms: no byte quota is published; the tunnel is a Cloudflare edge in front of a bundled cloudflared, so Cloudflare's terms and edge limits apply

interface_detail: nport 8080 registers a stable https://user-<n>.nport.link name and runs a bundled cloudflared tunnel to it
tooling: the nport npm CLI, which spawns a bundled cloudflared binary
chaining: it adds a stable name and a session cap over a Cloudflare quick tunnel rather than an independent relay network; a reader who excludes Cloudflare from the threat model excludes this too
binding_note: the 4-hour session cap fails first; the edge is Cloudflare's, so its limits also apply underneath.

identity_cost.detail: no sign-up: the page says 'No sign-up required', and the harness registered a tunnel with zero credentials

reliability_note: nport is a wrapper around cloudflared and the public edge is Cloudflare's, so an outage or a policy change at Cloudflare reaches it; the harness measured a 4-hour session cap
confidence_note: the no-sign-up and Cloudflare claims are read from the vendor page; the 4-hour cap is a sandbox measurement, so the record is reported

evidence.proved: the harness measured a 4-hour session cap

notes: A stable-name wrapper around a Cloudflare quick tunnel: the naming is its own, the edge is not. The 4-hour session cap and the Cloudflare dependency are the two facts a reader needs.
